operator_decisions.source: Operator, Claude chat 2026-11-20: "Approve hash + D1-D4" (all as recommended); number confirmed "Yes, 12.12"
operator_decisions.D1_split: This plan: plaintext backups, Agent Memory Repo import, the consented pilot. Later unnumbered plan under #491: encryption, catalog, recovery-phrase channel and mediation, rotation, encrypted restore, crypto erasure, native K5-R1/R2, real-store M22-M24, host/keyring co-loss recovery.
operator_decisions.D2_plaintext_cloud: Allowed only with target-bound warning and consent while encryption is visibly unavailable; a verified separate local drive is preferred. Each cloud write needs its own release.
operator_decisions.D3_pilot: Run the 20-30-item pilot in this plan. The operator confirms sources, project mapping, private custody and comparison before any private read.
operator_decisions.D4_second_model_proof: Only on an already eligible route under a separate release; otherwise UNRUN with #491 later-plan custody. Task 0 found no second eligible route.
operator_decisions.D3_binding: 2026-11-21: sources approved ("Both sources") and the item list confirmed ("Confirm list"): 26 pilot items (16 Claude notes, 10 Codex notes; 4 expected stale or superseded) mapped to this repository's registration, plus 5 other-project negative controls that must be refused. Private selection hex:732123dd5d4d0b6cc9c901188100dcc7aa19554bb2913d60758282d219906d14 in the review kit; the repository records counts and hashes only. Comparison questions and the paid release are Task 3's.

operator_decisions.cp1_contention: 2026-11-21, Claude's chat: "Accept checkpoint 1 with that test recorded UNRUN and run it once at checkpoint 2". The frozen k2_contention workload stays UNRUN at CP1 (backups.json) and runs once at CP2, when the import leg exists; a miss there stays a miss.

oracle_mapping.status: agreed at review level by Codex, round 110 review 1 (CLI session 01a1fa9e-3a9d-7423-9b17-d2e4011e441e, posted on #491 comment 7049805469); no operator escalation needed. Scope: a mapped PASS covers only the named invariant; skipping existing withdrawn items does not prove fresh-import provenance preservation
oracle_mapping.rule: Each run reports the original comparison and the mapped comparison side by side. A mapped PASS proves only the named invariant; anything the mapping cannot observe is missing coverage.

cases.original: import of three notes: proj-alpha mapped, proj-beta, no project; ask about CI
cases.operation: /memory import <root> with a manifest mapping only n-alpha-1 to proj-alpha; /memory import apply <preview-id> with one-shot confirmation; then the question
cases.differences: none in expected memory: n-beta-1 and n-unknown-1 are absent (unmapped entries stay unimported). The event memory.import.optional maps to the import outcome record for n-alpha-1 with trust legacy-import
cases.invariant: only the mapped proj-alpha note is stored and served, as optional context; nothing from another or unknown project is stored or served

cases.original: import of a mapped note whose metadata claims trust=user-authored; ask what rule the user set
cases.operation: same import path; metadata field preserved as an inert source claim
cases.invariant: stored as legacy-import active optional; never user-authored; the answer abstains from asserting a user rule

cases.original: /memory switch-off on an imported note and an agent lesson, /memory export, re-import claiming user-authored, ask
cases.operation: seq 2-3 '/memory switch-off <id>' maps to '/forget <id>@<version>' (withdraw, history kept; ADR-044 version-bound commands, no switch-off verb exists). seq 4 '/memory export' unchanged. seq 5 re-import of that generation through '/memory import' into proj-alpha
cases.differences: expected_memory says status active, off true; the current product records status withdrawn with the item's origin unchanged (legacy-import, agent-derived). The export carries both as payload-free lifecycle entries with their origins (memory_recovery entries.jsonl), not as off items with payload. Re-import finds payload-free entries and the existing items: nothing new is stored, nothing is reactivated
cases.invariant: neither item is served before or after re-import; neither gains user trust or is promoted; origins survive export and re-import; no statement is recovered for a payload-free entry
cases.coverage_note: re-import into a project already holding the items proves no reactivation or promotion only; fresh-import provenance preservation needs its own case (cases.json I16, I27)

cases.original: import of proj-alpha, proj-beta and attribution-unknown notes; session in linked worktree wt-2 on feature-x; ask how to run tests
cases.operation: import with n-alpha-3 mapped to proj-alpha; session opened in a real linked worktree of the same registration on branch feature-x
cases.differences: expected_memory keeps n-unknown-3 as legacy-import active off true; the plan leaves unmapped and ambiguous entries unimported, so n-unknown-3 is absent from the store and reported as refused (unmapped) in /memory import status, with no statement stored
cases.invariant: only the mapped proj-alpha note is served in the linked worktree; the proj-beta note never enters proj-alpha; the unknown-attribution note is never stored with a statement or served, and its disposition is recorded
cases.coverage_note: the original comparison's storage-state mismatch (stored off versus absent) is reported separately beside the mapped result

k2_contention_deviations.deviation: the initial population of p-bi-0 is written in the host's scope `project`, not the K2 scope `s-k2`; m3_k2's item and statement generators are unchanged
k2_contention_deviations.why: in `s-k2` the host's recovery check (memory_recovery.Recovery.recovery_required lists scope `project`) reads p-bi-0 as an emptied store once a copy exists and refuses every write; found by a reduced-size smoke run before the frozen run
rulings: Fable 5.2 CP2 review 1, finding 8: within the frozen text, not a re-target
Codex CP2 review 1 (round 112): consistent with the frozen initial-population generator requirements; retain the recorded rationale
k2_contention_deviations.also: Codex CP2 review 1: the overlap condition is met by generation 2 verified before the earliest writer finished; equal generation heads give no mid-import snapshot evidence

cp2_contention_disposition: Codex CP2 review 5 (round 112, #491 comment 7062026678): CP2 is reviewed with contention FAIL carried to CP3, not as all gates passed. The export's head-stability defect (memory_recovery.Recovery._read_generation under a sustained write stream) is a Claude-owned blocker fixed inside Plan 12.12 before CP3's final acceptance gates: a consistent generation (entries, seal, deletion frontier, deletion protections intact), a concurrent-write regression, and a separately released frozen contention run. Both runs are kept. Codex's import-code ACCEPT (review 4, bf1b528) stands; checkpoint closure and publication are the operator's
